That legislation is still pending with the state and with this lack of regulation, we are finding that some of the short-term rental owners not submitting their lodging taxes to the city income tax department which as you know by law is required these taxes are used to support nonprofits such as the Fairfield County Visitors Bureau and the Decorative Arts Center two agencies I think we can all agree help us create a solid economy in our downtown Lancaster the zoning office also receives several phone calls sporadically from interested parties that are trying to establish a short-term rental and they're just looking for some kind of guidance so I thought the best way to go through the code was just section by section 1131 this is what is required in the zoning clearance permit section a establishes that a zoning clearance permit is needed to operate a short-term rental in Lancaster the corresponding sections state that a separate permit will be needed for each dwelling unit and that a copy of that permit must be maintained and available on site. Section B establishes that each permit will be effective until December 31st of the calendar year of issuance. Section C states that a renewal application is due by the first Monday in November prior to the expiration date. Section 113102 establishes that the Mayor of Lancaster will determine the fee schedule and Section A states that any lodging tax will be paid directly to the City Income Tax Department. 11-3103 state our list our application requirements these are pretty standard of our zoning applications as well with things like the address of short-term rentals the type of dwelling the name of the contact information for the applicant the name of the local host or the emergency contact that can respond within an hour if they're different they're different individuals the maximum number of occupants that the applicant is trying to establish, and the maximum number of motor vehicles including garage space, two in the driveway, and two on street parking. A specific number of parking is not required in the Central Business District if the premises are within 1,000 feet of on street parking or public parking facility. The required off street and Central Business District parking aligns with our current zoning code Chapter 1143.11. It's also in our requirements to have a labeled site plan with an aerial photo that kind of identifies where these parking spaces will be and then a floor plan that shows the locations of the bedrooms. This will help with our occupancy and zoning compliance. It also requires a copy of the background check for the applicant, local host, and property manager if these are separate individuals. Section B establishes that any change in information in the application or renewal should be reported to our offices within 10 days of the change. Section C establishes that any change in owner or leaseholder shall void the current zoning permit. This aligns with our current standards that a new tenant or change of business would have to get new permits and occupancy. 11-3104 sets forth some standards for short-term rentals. On-site parking shall only be in spaces designated on approved site plan except for the central business district. No advertising or signage will appear on the exterior or on the exterior shall be permitted and then securities cameras shall be installed on the exterior of the property or in communal spaces such as living room or kitchen. No cameras shall be placed in bedrooms or bathrooms. The short-term rentals shall not house sex offenders, be rented by the hour, or used for any sexually oriented businesses. The short-term applicant, short-term rental applicant, must obtain an occupancy permit from the City Building Department prior to renting the premises. The occupancy permit will help establish compliance with state and local fire and building laws short-term rentals shall not adversely affect the character of the neighborhood in a manner that disturbs the peace and they must be maintained in a manner that remains free from zoning building or international property maintenance code violations the grounds for a denial of a permit would be if the applicant submits an incomplete application or renewal and or fails to pay the required fee if the applicant makes a material misrepresentation of facts if the short-term rental premises has pending zoning building or international property maintenance code or other regulatory violations or if the applicant or short-term rental premises have a documented history of nuisance behavior or criminal activity that endangers neighborhood or public safety 113106 is the revocation of a permit. This letter is written to you as concurrent commissioners of the Lancaster Park Board Commissioners to share my concerns regarding the lack of development of Bowers Memorial Park. It has been more than six years since the city accepted the donation of 20 plus acres of land from D. Merrill Bowers for development into Bowers Memorial Park. As you may know, I was instrumental in encouraging this donation from Mr. Bowers while I was a member of the Park Board and worked with several superintendents to complete the donation. It is an extreme disappointment to me that the Park Board has failed to move this forward with the development of the Bowers Memorial Park, originally envisioned as a replacement sports baseball park for Miller Park, which the city threatened and is now completed changing into the city water department plant. New ball diamonds were a priority. Although Mr. Bowers believed moving baseball diamonds to his donated land would solve the need for diamond relocation and the parts department developed a plan for installation of ball field complex, Mr. Bowers did not restrict his donation to the use of only ball fields. Shortly after the donation was accepted, There was an article in the Eagle Gazette about the donations and plans for the new work. Mike Tharp was quoted as saying the park should be ready for use by 2021. Obviously, this did not happen. The legal ownership documents require the land donated by Mr. Bowers and accepted by the city be used only as a public park and until development of the property conveyed to be used only as open green space for agricultural purposes. The park board has failed to follow through with the original plan, and by stopping midway in its regrading efforts, is not using the land as open green space for agriculture purposes, thus thwarting Mr. Bower's intentions. I do understand the issues faced by the park board for this project, COVID intervention, change of superintendents, diversion of funds when the purchase development of General Sherman property was undertaken, but six years is a long time wait to see some activity on a previously conceived project in addition the suspension of the initial grading of the property has left the property in an unsightly and deplorable condition and an eyesore to the neighborhood over the years since the donation i have spoken to mike tharp and steve gayfield about this project with various explanations giving for the delay in the development and assurances that the property is still going to be developed while i still believe there is a need for more baseball diamonds a city if a different use if a different park use this land is considered more desirable i urge you to move forward and at least restore the property to a cleaner more pleasant look but preferably to a timely developed bowers park into a park that will be a benefit to the community i also bring to your attention the donation of 786.47 that was was made to the Friends of the Parks in finalization of the Bowers estate and from the memorial donations made by Friends to be used as a plaque on the proposed shelter house with the inscription this property donated by D. Merrill Bowers for the enjoyment of the community. I hope that the Friends of the Parks have earmarked these funds for the purpose and someday in the foreseeable future such a plaque can be installed. It is a deterrent to future potential donors when accepting a gift the park board fails to follow through with the stated intentions in part motivated the gift. I urge you to honor the donation of Mr. Bowers by prioritizing the development of the land he donated into a park for the community good. That's signed Judith Edwards.
